correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, a Hilbert-space variance identity for n core and n leaf images gives VP<=aC², VQ>=9a, and matched-pair mean squared separation W<=C² with a=(n-1)/(2n). The reverse triangle inequality forces C²>=a(3-C)² if C<3, hence C>=3/(1+sqrt(2n/(n-1))); if C>=3 the bound is automatic. An explicit pair of homothetic regular simplices attains all metric inequalities: core-core c, leaf-leaf 3, matched c, off-diagonal cross sqrt(c²+3c) in [2,2c]. Equality in all bounds forces common centroids, exact pair classes and proportional centered simplices, yielding uniqueness up to congruence and dimension n-1. Standalone exact-algebra/decimal tests were executed for finite n, not substituted for the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The complete graph with one private pendant leaf at each vertex is a canonical infinite graph family. Its best Hilbert metric distortion is a natural functional-analytic invariant. The exact nontrivial formula holds for all clique sizes, has a sharp uniform asymptotic limit, and rigidly specifies every minimizing embedding and its affine dimension. This is more informative than finite examples, generic bounds or negative-type threshold tests; no arbitrary parameter slice is needed.
